acceptance: the skeleton decision came first: one is built only when the first paint waits for a named loading signal; none for a presentational, synchronous, already-loaded or parent-covered component
the skeleton is built from the shared Skeleton.vue primitive; no skeleton library and no hand-rolled pulsing div, and the primitive is created once in the ui layer if absent
the skeleton is a separate <Component>Skeleton.vue in the same folder as the real component and exported beside it; the real component has no loading branch of its own
it has the real component's shape, with shared sizes read from custom properties or tokens, so the content replaces it without a layout jump
the consumer picks between the two with v-if/v-else on the loading signal, or uses the skeleton as the Suspense #fallback
in Storybook the skeleton is shown under the real component in each state, with no story file of its own
